uncited: It differs from brute-force volume rendering by adapting the sampling density to the visual significance of the region, rather than processing every voxel at full resolution.
Inputs: A 3D volume dataset, camera parameters (position, orientation, projection), and a threshold for acceptable detail loss or projected pixel size.
- Volume data: 3D array of scalar or vector values.
- Texture blocks: Sub-volumes mapped to 2D texture objects.
Each block has a resolution level (e.g., $16^3$, $8^3$).
- LOD map: A 3D grid or hierarchical structure indicating the appropriate resolution level for each spatial region.
Determine the projected size of volume elements (voxels) on the screen for the current camera view.
For each region of the volume, calculate the local detail requirement based on gradient magnitude or opacity variance.
Select the lowest resolution texture block that satisfies the projected resolution constraint and local detail threshold.
Lower-resolution blocks require fewer fragment shader invocations per unit area.
Composite the fragments to produce the final image.
Let $P$ be the projected size of a voxel in pixels.
Let $T$ be the threshold for minimum projected size.
If $P < T$, a lower-resolution block is used.
The reduction in fragment shader load is proportional to the ratio of the original voxel count to the reduced block count.
- Threshold $T$: Not given in the sources.
- Precision issues may arise when transitioning between resolution levels, causing visible seams.
- Degenerate input: Regions with no detail may still be processed if the LOD map is not correctly initialized.
Time and memory complexity: Reduced fragment shader load compared to brute-force rendering.
Memory usage depends on the number of texture blocks and their resolutions.
Measured performance: Not given in the sources.
When to use: When fragment shader load is a bottleneck and volume detail varies spatially.
When not: When high fidelity is required everywhere or when hardware supports efficient brute-force rendering.

detail: Origin: Developed to reduce the load for fragment shaders on volume rendering hardware such as the VolumePro500 and VolumePro 1000 [S1, unofficial][S2, book].

The claim states that the method was developed to reduce the load for fragment shaders on volume rendering hardware such as the VolumePro500 and VolumePro 1000. Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly state that current research efforts have concentrated on reducing the load for fragment shaders in the context of specialized volume rendering hardware like the VolumePro500 and VolumePro 1000, and that level-of-detail methods (which rasterize lower-resolution texture blocks) were devised for this purpose.
Level-of-detail texture mapping reduces fragment shader load by rasterizing lower-resolution texture blocks whenever local volume detail or projected resolution allows [S1, unofficial][S2, book].
